text: {me} of {me.house} storms into the hall: "{suitor} of {rival.house} took my daughter {daughter} off the road at night. Forty riders, no banners. I want her back, and I want his head."

options.label: Order her sent back, and punish {suitor}
options.hint: {me.house} +15 · {rival.house} −20 · {rival} will call it the crown meddling in a love match

memory.rival: The King shamed my son {suitor} in front of the whole realm.

options.text: On the King's order, {daughter} goes back to {me.house}. {suitor} is as good as sent to the Wall.

options.label: They're married. Make it lawful

memory.me: The King blessed the man who stole my daughter.

options.text: The King declares {daughter} and {suitor} lawfully married. {me} leaves court without a word.

options.label: Let {me.house} take her back by force
options.hint: {me.house} and {rival.house} go to war, but the crown keeps its hands clean
options.text: The King says a {me.father} may fetch {me.his} own daughter. {me.house} calls up its banners.

text: {heir}, heir of {me.house}, has run off with a girl of {rival.house}. {me} wants the King's men to bring the young fool home. {rival} says {rival.his} house has been shamed, and wants blood.

options.label: Bring {heir} home in chains

memory.heir: The King dragged me home in chains.

options.text: The King's riders bring {heir} home in chains. The girl is sent back to {rival.house}, her name ruined.

options.label: Let them be together
options.hint: {me.house} and {rival.house} drawn together · both lords −10, both furious
options.text: The King leaves the pair alone. Both fathers rage, but slowly they start to talk.

options.label: Pay {rival.house} for the insult (120 gold)
options.text: The crown pays {rival.house} for its daughter's honour. That settles it, at least on paper.

text: Your spymaster says {bannerman}, sworn to {me.house}, was seen at a border inn with men in {rival.house}'s colours. Money changed hands. {me} doesn't know yet.

options.label: Tell {me}

memory.bannerman: Someone told my lord about the inn. I know it was the crown.

options.text: The King sends word to {me}. {bannerman} is called to {bannerman.his} lord's hall and doesn't come out for three days.

options.label: Make {bannerman} the crown's spy (80 gold)
options.hint: You'll know what {rival.house} plans, but if it comes out, both houses will hate you

memory.bannerman: I serve the King now, whoever else I smile at.

options.text: {bannerman} is quietly bought. {bannerman.He} keeps meeting {rival.house}'s men, and now {bannerman.he} tells the King what they say.

options.label: Watch and say nothing
options.hint: It costs nothing, but if {bannerman} changes sides, {bannerman.his} town goes with {bannerman.his} coat
options.text: The King watches. {bannerman} rides home to {me.house}, smiling.

text: A raven caught on the Kingsroad: {me} of {me.house} and {friend} of {friend.house} have sworn a pact and sealed it with a marriage contract. The letter doesn't mention the King at all.

options.label: Bless the alliance in public
options.hint: Both +10 · two houses stand together, for or against you
options.text: The King blesses the pact between {me.house} and {friend.house} in front of the whole court, as if it were his idea.

options.label: Forbid it
options.hint: Both −15 · the pact is broken, and both lords suspect the other betrayed it
options.text: The King forbids the pact. Each lord is sure the other leaked the letter.

options.label: Warn {rival.house} and let them deal with it
options.text: A copy of the letter reaches {rival}. The realm grows tense.

text: {me} of {me.house} asks the King's leave to march on {rivalTown}: "{rival} burns my villages and laughs at your peace. Let me march, or give me justice."

options.label: Let them march
options.text: The King lets {me} march. The banners of {me.house} go up across the land.

options.label: Forbid it, on pain of treason
options.hint: {me.house} −20 · {me} may march anyway, without your blessing

me.text: settle things with {rival.house} my own way

options.text: The King forbids the march. {me} bows stiffly, but nobody thinks it's over.

options.label: Call both lords in and set the terms (150 gold)
options.text: Both lords kneel at Kingsmere and swear to keep the King's peace. The crown pays for the burned villages.

text: {me} has already sent riders into {rival.house}'s lands. Now {me} asks the King to look away: "Just a small fire, Your Grace. They started it."

options.label: Look the other way
options.hint: {rivalTown} is raided · {me.house} +10 · {rival.house} −15 when they learn of it
options.text: The King looks the other way. {rivalTown} burns, and its men are buried.

options.label: Call the riders back
options.text: The King's herald catches {me.house}'s riders on the road. They turn back, cursing.

options.label: Fine {me.house} for breaking the peace
options.text: The King fines {me.house} for its riders. The silver comes late, and short.

text: {heir}, heir of {me.house}, fell ill at a feast held by {rival.house}. The physician says it was poison. {me} wants {rival} tried for murder. {rival} swears on the old gods it was bad fish.

options.label: Put {rival} on trial
options.hint: {rival.house} −30 · {me.house} +15 · if innocent, the realm sees a tyrant

memory.rival: The King put me on trial over a sick boy and a bad fish.

options.text: {rival} stands trial at Kingsmere. Nothing is proven, but nobody forgets it.

options.label: Send the royal physician to save {heir} (80 gold)
options.hint: {heir} lives · {me.house} +10 · the question is left open

memory.heir: The King's physician saved my life.

options.text: The royal physician rides all night. {heir} lives, pale and thin, and remembers who saved them.

options.label: It was just bad fish

dies.text: {heir}, heir of {me.house}, dies of the fever. {me} names the poisoner in every hall.

options.text: The King does nothing.

text: A boy of fourteen stands in the hall with {bannerman}'s face but not {bannerman.his} name. {bannerman} asks the King to make him legitimate. {me}'s trueborn family is outraged.

options.label: Make him legitimate

memory.bannerman: The King gave my child a name.

options.text: By royal decree, the boy is trueborn. {bannerman} weeps in the hall.

options.label: A bastard stays a bastard
options.text: The King refuses. The boy keeps the name Snow, and {bannerman} stays angry.

options.label: Take the boy into the King's service
options.hint: The crown gains a sworn sword, and {bannerman} is grateful, but you'll have to watch him
options.text: The boy joins the King's service. He swears his oath in front of the whole court.

text: {me} of {me.house} offers {heir} as a ward at Kingsmere, as proof of loyalty. Your council thinks it's a way to put eyes at court.

options.label: Take {heir} as a ward
options.hint: {me.house} +15 · {me} cannot rise while you hold the child
options.text: {heir} comes to Kingsmere and kneels before the throne. The court watches the newcomer closely.

options.label: The crown doesn't need hostages
options.hint: {me.house} −10 · a gesture refused is an insult
options.text: The King turns down the ward. {me} takes it as an insult, and it is one.

text: {me} of {me.house} offers to hold a great tourney at {town} in the King's honour, if the crown pays for the prizes.

options.label: Pay for the tourney (200 gold)
options.hint: Every house +5 · {me.house} +15 · knights flock to the crown
options.text: Everyone in the realm talks about the tourney at {town}. Two hedge knights earn their spurs and swear to the King.

options.label: Let {me.house} pay for it
options.text: {me.house} hosts the tourney at its own cost, and makes sure everyone knows it.

options.label: No time for games
options.text: The King has no time for tourneys. The knights go home disappointed.

text: A sellsword captain called the Golden Wolf offers five hundred men to whoever pays first. {me} of {me.house} is already bidding.

options.label: Outbid {me} (250 gold)
options.text: The Golden Wolf takes the King's silver. His men camp outside Kingsmere.

options.label: Let {me.house} have them
options.text: The sellswords march under {me.house}'s banner. The other houses count them nervously.

options.label: Send them out of the realm
options.text: The King orders the sellswords out of the realm. They head east, looking for another war.

text: Sickness has come to {town}. {me} of {me.house} wants to shut the gates and let it burn itself out. The priests say that's murder.

options.label: Shut the gates
options.hint: The sickness stays inside {town}, and the poor of {town} never forgive it

memory.me: I shut the gates of {town} on my own people, with the King's leave.

options.text: The gates of {town} close. For a season, nobody goes in or out.

options.label: Send healers and grain (150 gold)
options.text: The crown sends healers and grain to {town}. Some of the healers don't come back.

options.label: Burn the sick quarter
options.hint: Brutal and certain · {me.house} −10 · the realm whispers about the King
options.text: The sick quarter of {town} burns. The sickness ends, and so does the King's name for mercy.

text: {me}, a pious lord, accuses {rival} of {rival.house} of secretly worshipping the old gods: weirwoods, blood, and sacrifices at night.

options.label: Condemn {rival} as a heretic

memory.rival: The King branded me a heretic on the word of a zealot.

options.text: The King condemns {rival}'s gods. The weirwoods of {rival.house} are cut down.

options.label: Let every lord keep his own gods
options.text: The King says every house may keep its own gods. {me} prays for the King's soul.

text: A knight of {rival.house} has fled to {me.house} with his whole household, saying {rival} meant to hang him. {rival} wants him back for trial.

options.label: Let {me.house} keep him
options.text: The knight swears to {me.house}. {rival} sends a raven nobody dares read out loud.

options.label: Send him back to {rival}
options.text: The knight is sent back in chains. He hangs within the week.

options.label: He serves the crown now
options.hint: The crown gains a knight · both −5
options.text: The King takes the knight into his own service, and both lords feel cheated.

text: {me} of {me.house} says {rival.house} never paid the dowry it promised for a marriage ten years ago. With interest, {rival.house} owes 200 gold.

options.label: Order {rival.house} to pay
options.text: {rival.house} pays the old dowry. Every coin is counted twice.

options.label: Split the difference
options.text: The King splits the debt down the middle. Neither house is happy.

options.label: Ten years is too late
options.text: The King throws out the claim. {me} grumbles that the crown forgets its promises.

text: {bannerman} of {me.house} was killed on a hunt in {rival.house}'s woods, by an arrow in the back. {rival}'s men say it was a stray. {me} says it was murder.

options.label: Make {rival.house} pay a blood price
options.text: {rival.house} pays the blood price for {bannerman}. Nobody ever explains the arrow.

options.label: Call it an accident
options.text: The King rules it an accident. {me.house} rides home in silence.

options.label: Send the King's justice to find out (60 gold)
options.hint: Both −5 · the truth comes out, one way or another
options.text: The King's justice finds the bowman. He hangs without naming anyone.

text: {me.house} has had the best harvest anyone can remember. {me} offers to sell the extra to the crown, or to the highest bidder across the sea.

options.label: Buy it for the royal granaries (120 gold)
options.text: The King's granaries fill with {me.house}'s grain.

options.label: Tax the windfall
options.text: The King taxes the harvest. {me} pays, and doesn't forget.

options.label: Let them sell abroad
options.text: {me.house}'s grain sails across the sea, and its coffers fill.

text: {bannerman}, sworn to {me.house}, goes over {bannerman.his} lord's head to the King: "{me} took my best fields for {me.his} own child. I served thirty years. Is this my reward?"

options.label: Rule for {bannerman}

memory.bannerman: The King stood by me against my own lord.

options.text: The King gives {bannerman}'s fields back. {me} won't forget who went over {me.his} head.

options.label: A lord's land is his to give

bannerman.text: find a lord who keeps faith

options.text: The King sides with {me}. {bannerman} rides home with nothing.

text: {me} of {me.house} is {me.age} and forgets {me.his} own children's names. {heir} asks the King to let them rule now, before the house falls apart.

options.label: Let {heir} rule
options.hint: {heir} owes the crown, but {me} is shamed

memory.me: The King let my own child push me aside.

options.text: The King names {heir} to run {me.house} in {me.his} name. The old {me.lord} sits by the fire and doesn't understand.

options.label: A lord rules until he dies
options.text: The King says no. {heir} leaves court with dark thoughts.

text: Hill clans have crossed into {me.house}'s lands near {town}. Thousands of them, starving, with children. They say something worse is coming behind them.

options.label: Let them settle the empty land
options.text: The clansfolk settle the empty hills by {town}. {me} puts guards on every road.

options.label: Drive them back (80 gold)
options.hint: {me.house} +5 · the riders are the crown's to pay · they will come back angrier
options.text: {me.house}'s riders drive the clansfolk back into the snow.

options.label: Take their fighters into the King's army
options.text: The clan fighters swear to the King. Their families go south with them.

text: {rival.house} has put a toll on the only bridge between {me.house}'s lands and the Kingsroad. {me} calls it robbery.

options.label: Scrap the toll
options.text: The King scraps the toll. {rival}'s men pull down the gate, slowly.

options.label: The crown takes half
options.hint: The crown gains 80 gold from {rival.house} · both −5
options.text: The toll stays, and the King takes his cut. Now everyone pays.

options.label: A lord may toll his own bridge
options.text: The toll stays. {me.house}'s carts go the long way round.

text: Fishermen in {me.house}'s lands have pulled a stone egg out of the sea, and it's warm to the touch. {me} offers it to the King, or to whoever pays most.

options.label: Buy it (200 gold)
options.text: The egg comes to Kingsmere and sits beside the throne. The court swears it moves at night.

options.label: Take it, by right
options.text: The King takes the egg as his right. {me} hands it over with a face like stone.

options.label: Let {me.house} keep it
options.hint: {me.house} +10 · and a house with a dragon egg starts to dream

me.text: hatch the egg and take the throne

options.text: {me.house} keeps the egg. Its lord has started reading old histories.

text: {rival.house}'s envoy mocked {me}'s dead {me.wife} at a feast in your hall. {me} has demanded satisfaction, and both are reaching for their swords.

options.label: Let them fight it out
options.hint: One may die · the winner's house +10
options.text: Swords out in the King's hall. The envoy bleeds on the floor, and {me.house} is satisfied.

options.label: Throw the envoy out
options.text: The King throws {rival.house}'s envoy out of court.

options.label: Make them both apologise
options.text: Both men apologise through gritted teeth. The feast never recovers.

text: Silver has been found in the hills near {town}. {me} of {me.house} asks for the mining rights, which by old law belong to the crown.

options.label: Give them the rights
options.text: The King gives {me.house} the silver of {town}. The house grows fat.

options.label: The crown keeps them
options.text: The crown's miners arrive at {town}. {me.house} watches its silver go to Kingsmere.

options.label: Share the silver
options.text: The crown and the house share the silver of {town}.

text: Forty men ran away from the King's levy and are hiding in {town}. {me} of {me.house} won't hand them over: "They're my men first."

options.label: Demand them, and hang them
options.text: The deserters are handed over and hanged at the crossroads. The levies stop running.

options.label: Pardon them and send them back (50 gold)
options.hint: The crown gains men, and pays to rearm them · {me.house} +5
options.text: The deserters are pardoned and march back to the King's banner.

options.label: Let {me.house} keep them
options.hint: {me.house} +10 · the King's levy is a joke
options.text: The deserters stay in {town}. Now every lord knows the King's levy is optional.

text: {me} of {me.house} thinks {me.his} {me.wife} has been passing {me.house}'s secrets to {rival} of {rival.house}. {me} wants the marriage ended, and {rival} named in front of the court.

options.label: End the marriage
options.text: The marriage is ended. {rival}'s name is in every tavern.

options.label: Refuse without proof

me.text: catch {rival} and my {me.wife} at their letters

options.text: The King refuses. {me} pays men to follow {me.his} own {me.wife}.

options.label: Let the Archbishop decide
options.hint: Both −3 · it drags on for years
options.text: The matter goes to the Faith, where it will take years.

text: {me} of {me.house} wants {daughter} to marry into the royal family. It would tie {me.house} to the crown and raise it above every other house.

options.label: Accept the match
options.text: {daughter} of {me.house} is promised to the royal family. The other houses smile and seethe.

options.label: Say no, gently
options.text: The King says no, with gifts. {me} isn't comforted.

text: {me} of {me.house} has refused the King's call for soldiers: "My men are needed for the harvest." Your council says it's a test of your power.

options.label: Send royal troops to fetch them
options.text: Royal troops ride into {me.house}'s lands and march the levies out at spearpoint.

options.label: Accept the excuse
options.hint: {me.house} +5 · other houses learn they can refuse
options.text: The King accepts {me}'s excuse. The other lords take note.

options.label: Take gold instead of men
options.text: {me.house} pays in silver instead of men. The King hires his own soldiers.

text: A man of {rival.house} was caught copying letters in {me}'s private rooms. Under questioning he says {rival} sent him to find proof that {me} is plotting against the crown.

options.label: Investigate {me}
options.text: The King opens an inquiry into {me}. {rival} looks very pleased.

options.label: Hang the spy
options.text: The spy hangs from {me.house}'s walls. {rival} says nothing.

options.label: Give him fake letters and send him back
options.hint: Both houses trust each other less, and the crown watches
options.text: The spy goes home with forged letters. {rival} reads them very carefully.

text: Fire has burned out the lower town of {town}. {me} of {me.house} asks for help to rebuild before winter.

options.label: Rebuild it (180 gold)
options.text: The crown pays to rebuild {town}. New timber goes up before the snow.

options.label: Make the other houses pay their share
options.text: Every great house sends silver for {town}. None of them gladly.

options.label: Fires happen
options.text: The King sends his sympathy. {town} spends the winter in tents.

text: {heir} of {me.house} has challenged {rival}'s champion to a duel in front of the court, to settle their house's honour.

options.label: Allow the duel
options.hint: {heir} may win great honour, or die

dies.text: {heir} of {me.house} falls in the duel in front of the court. {me} carries the body home.

options.text: Swords ring out in the yard at Kingsmere.

options.label: Forbid it
options.text: The King forbids the duel. {heir} calls it cowardice, loud enough to be heard.

text: Island raiders are hitting {me.house}'s coast near {town}. {me} wants the royal fleet, and also wants to know why the crown keeps a fleet at all.

options.label: Send the fleet (150 gold)
options.text: The royal fleet drives the raiders off {me.house}'s coast.

options.label: Let {me.house} build its own ships
options.text: {me.house} sets up its own coast watch.

options.label: Pay the raiders to leave (80 gold)
options.text: The raiders take the King's silver and sail away, laughing.

text: {me} of {me.house} is very ill and asks the King to swear, in front of witnesses, to protect {me.his} house after {me.he} dies.

options.label: Swear it
options.hint: {me.house} +20 · and you are bound by it

memory.me: The King swore to protect my house.

options.text: The King swears, in front of the whole court, to protect {me.house}.

options.label: Kind words, but no oath
options.text: The King offers comfort, but no oath. {me} understands.

text: {me} of {me.house} brings you a letter: {rival} of {rival.house} asked {me.house} to join a rising against the crown. {me} said no, and came to you.

options.label: Reward {me} for staying loyal (100 gold)
options.text: The King rewards {me.house} in public. {rival} knows exactly why.

options.label: Strike {rival.house} first
options.hint: War: {me.house} marches on {rival.house} in your name
options.text: The King names {rival} a traitor. {me.house} marches in the crown's name.

options.label: Keep it quiet and watch (60 gold)
options.hint: {me.house} +5 · a watcher on {rival}, paid by the crown · {rival} does not know you know
options.text: The King thanks {me} and burns the letter. The court never hears of it.
